title: MPCD methodology
author: MPCD project team
institution: Ruhr University Bochum; Freie Universität Berlin; University of Cologne
primary_evidence: Separates manuscript transliteration, phonemic transcription, lemma, morphology, contextual senses and Avestan links. Experts revise pre-annotation; automatic and manual annotations remain distinguishable.
translation_implication: Preserve aligned representation layers and evidence status; attach contextual senses and source-language quotation links.
limitations: Methodology and working annotations are not a guarantee that every corpus entry is final or available as translation training data.

title: A Suggestion for the Transliteration of Middle Persian Texts in MPCD: A Three Layered Transliteration System (2020)
author: Kianoosh Rezania
primary_evidence: Explains that conventional transliteration already embeds etymological and interpretive choices. Distinguishes stored, representational and computational transliterations; the last intentionally collapses distinctions for searches.
translation_implication: Record the input convention and retain originals. A search-normalized match must not silently overwrite the philological reading.
limitations: A proposed scholarly encoding system, not proof that all ambiguities can be mechanically resolved; PDF character extraction is unsuitable for implementing its tables without visual checking.

title: HUZWĀREŠ
author: Desmond Durkin-Meisterernst
institution: Berlin-Brandenburg Academy of Sciences and Humanities, Turfan research
primary_evidence: Aramaic-derived written forms represent Middle Persian words. Scholarly transliteration distinguishes heterograms and phonetic material, including Iranian complements; phonemic transcription can conceal the original spelling.
translation_implication: Annotate heterogram, Iranian reading and grammatical complement separately; never translate every written form as ordinary Aramaic.
limitations: Conventions differ by edition; its examples do not exhaust heterograms or every possible reading. Institutional staff page establishes affiliation, not current availability.

title: IRAN vi. Iranian Languages and Scripts (3): Writing Systems
author: Prods Oktor Skjærvø
institution: Harvard University, Aga Khan Professor of Iranian Studies Emeritus
primary_evidence: Book Pahlavi merges historically different letters into common forms; words and context are needed for readings. Distinguishes writing traditions rather than equating them with one transparent alphabet.
translation_implication: Supplied script can remain linguistically underdetermined. Track script and representation type; allow multiple readings until context discriminates them.
limitations: This is a linguistic requirement, not a request for OCR. A supplied expert transcription may already resolve some written ambiguity.

title: FRAHANG Ī PAHLAWĪG
category: Authored scholarly encyclopedia: historical dictionary criticism
author: David Neil MacKenzie
institution: University of Göttingen, former Chair of Iranian Studies
primary_evidence: Describes the historical heterogram glossary and its variant recensions. Warns that mistaken interpretations entered later editions, including modern-language scholarship.
translation_implication: Dictionary entries need edition, attestation and uncertainty; agreement among derivative dictionaries is not independent evidence.
limitations: The historical Frahang is not a comprehensive modern Pahlavi dictionary. Criticisms concern specific editorial lineages, not every entry.

title: Universal Dependencies: Middle Persian language documentation
author: Universal Dependencies Middle Persian contributors
institution: Universal Dependencies; related grammatical research verified at Ruhr University Bochum
primary_evidence: Documents omitted arguments, ergative agreement, contextual active/passive interpretation, resumptive pronouns and underspecified coordination. Nominal gender is generally unmarked and plural marking optional; some tags encode editorial interpretations.
translation_implication: Annotate argument roles, coreference, omitted constituents, aspect and discourse relations; separate grammatical features from inferred target-language choices.
limitations: An annotation scheme embodies analytical choices. Its page does not identify an individual author; Thomas Jügel is a cited scholar, not asserted sole page author.

title: Die Entwicklung der Ergativkonstruktion im Alt- und Mitteliranischen (2015)
category: Scholarly grammar monograph; publisher synopsis inspected
author: Thomas Jügel
institution: Ruhr University Bochum; earlier doctoral research at Goethe University Frankfurt
primary_evidence: Publisher describes corpus-based analysis of approximately 12,500 Middle Persian examples, treating case, agreement, word order, omitted constituents, reflexivity, tense/aspect and enclitic pronouns.
translation_implication: Use corpus-attested grammatical analyses and counterexamples when adjudicating who did what; do not import Modern Persian parsing assumptions wholesale.
limitations: Only public synopsis/bibliography inspected, not the complete book. The numerical count is scholarly examples, not parallel translation pairs.

title: Zoroastrian ritual and exegetical traditions: the case of the Iranian Pahlavi Yasna
author: Mehrbod Khanizadeh
primary_evidence: Re-examines colophons through variant witnesses, parallels, syntax and context. An omitted object with nibišt ēstād permits active interpretation; competing reflexive antecedents alter who copied a text.
translation_implication: Keep alternative parses, coreference and supplied words visible, and cite the textual evidence used to choose among them.
limitations: These are argued scholarly interpretations of particular passages, not universal parsing rules. Journal issue is 2021; online publication is 2022.

title: EXEGESIS i. In Zoroastrianism
category: Authored scholarly encyclopedia: translation and commentary
author: Philip G. Kreyenbroek
institution: University of Göttingen, former Professor and Director of Iranian Studies
primary_evidence: Zand can preserve Avestan word order and fixed lexical renderings unlike idiomatic Middle Persian; explanatory comments and different teachers' judgments can coexist in the transmitted text.
translation_implication: Label quotation, inherited translation, paraphrase and commentary; preserve speaker/authority and disagreement rather than synthesizing one doctrinal statement.
limitations: Historical explanations are scholarly reconstruction. The task is to translate the supplied Pahlavi interpretation, not silently replace it with a modern Avestan translation.

title: MĀDAYĀN Ī HAZĀR DĀDESTĀN
category: Authored scholarly encyclopedia by specialist editor: legal philology
author: Maria Macuch
institution: Freie Universität Berlin, Institute of Iranian Studies
primary_evidence: The lawbook has a single incomplete manuscript, disturbed folio order, technical vocabulary and complex ambiguous syntax. Actual/hypothetical cases and competing juristic opinions are presented together. Distinguishes property substance from usufruct in different pledge institutions.
translation_implication: Record witness/order, hypothetical scope, legal roles and institutional definitions. Preserve distinctions that familiar English or Farsi labels can erase.
limitations: A specialist legal corpus differs from other Pahlavi genres; single-witness uncertainty cannot always be resolved by collation.

title: MIDDLE PERSIAN i. Pahlavi Literature
category: Authored scholarly encyclopedia: genres and transmission
author: Carlo Giovanni Cereti
institution: Sapienza University of Rome, full professor of Iranian Philology, Religions and History
primary_evidence: Describes religious, didactic, wisdom and courtly texts, differing styles and manuscript dependence. Later compilations preserve earlier material; genre boundaries are not always sharp.
translation_implication: Tag genre, textual layer and date range independently. Use register-sensitive senses and references rather than one style for every work.
limitations: A survey is not an authoritative edition of each passage. Composition, compilation and manuscript-copy dates must not be conflated.

title: GĒTĪG AND MĒNŌG
category: Authored scholarly encyclopedia: religious conceptual semantics
author: Shaul Shaked
institution: Hebrew University of Jerusalem, former professor
primary_evidence: Explains visible/material and invisible/mental modes of existence, their changing relations and textual variation. The distinction is not simply the identification of matter with evil found in some other systems.
translation_implication: Maintain domain concepts and context-specific renderings; avoid importing a modern or neighboring religion's conceptual opposition.
limitations: Terminology varies across texts and periods. A general theological summary cannot override an individual passage's evidence.
